name: Czechoslovak Republic

areaKm2.note: League of Nations Statistical Year-Book 1939/40, Table 2: Czecho-Slovakia 140 thousand km2 within the 1937 boundaries (low, mid). world_1930 Czechoslovakia polygon = 141,071 km2 computed by the pipeline (high). Pre-Munich territory incl. the Sudetenland and Carpathian Ruthenia; the world_1938 polygon (90,899 km2) already shows the post-Munich state and is not used.

population.note: League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40, Table 2: official estimate vi.1937 = 15,239k, 1937 estimate column 15,270k (mid); census 1.xii.1930 = 14,729k. COW NMC v7 tpop 1937 = 15,250k. OWID Czechoslovakia 1938 = 14.60M (low; COW 1938 also 14,600k, already net of the Munich cessions). High allows for growth to September 1938.

urbanization.note: HYDE 3.5 (OWID) urban share, present-day borders: Czechia 1930 36%, 1940 42%; Slovakia 1930 15%, 1940 20%. Weighted by OWID 1938 population (Czechia 10.88M, Slovakia 3.29M): 1930 = 0.31 (low), 1940 = 0.37 (high), ~0.35 in 1938 (mid); rural Ruthenia (~0.7M) is outside both series. COW upop/tpop 1937 = 1,619/15,250 = 0.11 counts cities over 100,000 only and is not used.

activePersonnel.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): strength after the general mobilisation of 23 September 1938 = 1,280,000 men (mid, Shishkin); the same page gives "about 1.5 million" in 42 divisions (high) and the 1936 mobilisation plan figure of 972,747 men (low). Peacetime army 200,000 (17 infantry and 4 mobile divisions). COW NMC v7 milper 1938 = 163k is an annual peacetime average. Snapshot date 30 September 1938. Grade C, not B: the source is a self-published compilation, and the primary works it cites (Shishkin, Osprey MAA 554) were not checked.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. After the general mobilisation of 23 September 1938 nearly every trained class was with its unit; older classes and State Defence Guard (SOS) men not yet called are counted here.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Everything outside the P roles in the 1.28M mobilised army: 2,330 guns, 1,177 AT guns, 1,379 mortars and the AA arm (272 heavy and 227 light AA guns), 80 engineer companies, the air force (6 regiments, ~1,300 aircraft), signals, fortress artillery, 17 armoured trains, trains and services (equipment counts from Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45)). Roughly 45% of the mobilised strength, the share in the Polish 1939 snapshot.

mobilizationRatio.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): 972,747 (1936 plan) to 1,280,000 (mobilised) and ~1.5M of ~15.2M = 0.064-0.1; mid 0.085 = 1.28M plus the remaining reserve classes. Reconstruction from the cited mobilisation figures.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Rifle strength of the mobilised army: 42 divisions in all, 4 of them mobile (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45)), so ~34 infantry divisions and division-size border groups at 9 battalions of ~900 rifles = ~275,000, plus fortress infantry of the border line (~50,000).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: vz.24 Mauser rifles, ZB vz.26 light and ZB-53 heavy machine guns, 81 mm mortars and 37 mm AT guns (995 vz.37 and 182 vz.34 in 1938), all domestic designs (cited samlib page).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training). Evidence: two-year service reintroduced after the 1934 rearmament decision; reservists recalled in May and September 1938 (cited samlib page).

count.note: Educated guess. Mountain brigades (Slovakia), cyclist battalions and the 31 border battalions formed in 1936 from Finance Guard, police, gendarmerie and 30,000 SOS reservists (cited samlib page, MAA 554).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: rifles and light machine guns, few heavy weapons in the SOS battalions.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5 for the police and SOS men, 0.5-0.75 for the mountain troops.

count.note: Educated guess. Mounted part of the four mobile divisions (13 dragoon regiments from 1936; a mobile division had 11,135 men in all, cited samlib page), about a third of each division.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: carbines, light machine guns and 37 mm AT guns; horse-mounted.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: long-service cadre; the mobile divisions fought the Sudeten German Freikorps in September 1938 (MAA 554 via the cited page).

count.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): 348 tanks and 73 tankettes in 1938 (Shishkin); by type 298 LT vz.35 (296-298), 50 LT vz.34, 7 Renault FT and 73 Tancik vz.33. 244 LT vz.35 were with the four mobile divisions in September 1938. Mid and high count tanks plus tankettes, low tanks only; the LT vz.38 was not yet delivered. Grade C, not B: the source is a self-published compilation, and the primary works it cites (Shishkin, Osprey MAA 554) were not checked.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: LT vz.35 (10 t, 37 mm gun, 25 mm armour) matched the Panzer II and served the Wehrmacht as Pz 35(t) in 1939-41; tankettes and FT obsolete.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: the tank brigade was formed only on 15 September 1935 and the LT vz.35 arrived mostly in 1937 (cited page); no combat experience.

count.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): 1,662 light field and mountain, 617 heavy and 51 super-heavy guns, howitzers and mortars = 2,330 (mid, high); low without the super-heavy pieces. 1,177 37 mm AT guns, 222 fortress 47 mm AT guns and 1,379 infantry mortars not counted. Grade C, not B: the source is a self-published compilation, and the primary works it cites (Shishkin, Osprey MAA 554) were not checked.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: new 105 mm vz.35 guns and 100 mm vz.30 howitzers alongside upgraded vz.14/19 and 150 mm vz.25 pieces (cited page); no regimental guns.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Austro-Hungarian and French-trained gunners; partly motorised heavy regiments.

count.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): 443 fighters in 1938, all Avia B.534 / Bk.534 biplanes, of which 219 were with combat units (low, mid); high = whole inventory. Grade C, not B: the source is a self-published compilation, and the primary works it cites (Shishkin, Osprey MAA 554) were not checked.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: B.534 biplane, 394 km/h, against the Bf 109 (cited page); the B.35 monoplane first flew only at the end of September 1938.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: two-year air force training by the late 1930s; Goering in 1936 rated the personnel among the leading air forces (cited page).

count.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): 187 bombers (147 with combat units: ~60 Tupolev SB-2/B-71, 67 Aero MB.200, 60 Aero Ab.101 in the inventory); mid = all bombers. High adds the 251 Letov S.328 reconnaissance-bombers with combat units (of 483 reconnaissance aircraft), which could carry 0.5 t of bombs. Grade C, not B: the source is a self-published compilation, and the primary works it cites (Shishkin, Osprey MAA 554) were not checked.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: SB-2 modern (430 km/h); MB.200 and Ab.101 obsolescent.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: as fighters.

count.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): AA batteries. 54 AA artillery batteries with 272 guns of 75-90 mm (low) + 11 AA companies with 20 mm Oerlikon guns (mid = 65) + 48 AA machine-gun companies (high = 113). 227 20 mm guns in all. Grade C, not B: the source is a self-published compilation, and the primary works it cites (Shishkin, Osprey MAA 554) were not checked.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: 272 medium AA guns and 227 20 mm guns for the whole state, mostly static around key sites; little mobile divisional AA (cited page).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: territorial AA organised in 4 zones and 21 groups around key sites.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: French-trained general staff under Krejci; partial mobilisation in May and general mobilisation in September 1938 completed in days; untested in war, and a defensive plan that relied on French and Soviet help (cited samlib page).

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5 (national conscript army) minus minorities. Evidence: the 1936 mobilisation plan counted 718,230 Slavs, 192,844 Germans and 61,671 Hungarians, i.e. a quarter of the mobilised men from minorities whose loyalty was doubtful (cited samlib page).

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 (motivated). Evidence: Czech and Slovak reservists answered the September 1938 call-up in full; defence of the homeland behind a new fortified line; German and Hungarian reservists less willing.

weapons.note: Anchor: between 7 (1905) and 8 (1943). Evidence: ZB vz.26 and ZB-53 machine guns, 37 mm vz.37 AT gun, 105 mm vz.35 gun, 81 mm mortars, ZK-383 SMG entering service (cited samlib page).

armor.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8 (rolled homogeneous armour). Evidence: LT vz.35 riveted 25 mm armour with a 37 mm gun; LT vz.38 not yet in service.

ships.note: Anchor: 7. No sea-going navy; a river flotilla of two artillery boats and patrol craft under the engineers (cited samlib page). Value only matters if ships are added.

fortification.note: Anchor: 8 = concrete lines (Maginot). Evidence: by September 1938 264 heavy blockhouses and 10,014 light pillboxes, a line modelled on the Maginot Line, about 20% of the planned heavy and 70% of the light objects (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czechoslovak_border_fortifications).

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways) toward 8 (motor transport). Evidence: 26,000 motor vehicles and tractors and 217,000 horses after mobilisation (cited samlib page); 13,548 km of railway.

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (telephone), radio partly. Evidence: signal battalions at army and corps level; radio below divisional level scarce (inferred from the organisation tables on the cited samlib page).

isr.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: 22 reconnaissance squadrons with 483 aircraft, sound-ranging; no radar.

air.note: Anchor: between 7 (1914) and 8 (1943). Evidence: B.534 biplane fighters, SB-2 monoplane bombers; no modern monoplane fighter in service.

cyber.note: No military computer networks before ~1990 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV) Czechoslovakia: 1937 = 4,594 (mid, high), 1936 = 4,143 (low), 2011 int$. No 1938 value.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Global Military Spending Dataset via OWID, Czechoslovakia: 1937 = 3.08% (low), 1938 = 4.36% (mid), 1939 = 5.32% (high). Mobilised but not at war on the snapshot date, so the 1938 annual share is the mid. COW milex 1938 = 201,459 thousand current US$, 1937 = 156,591.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry and mining share of output. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Czechoslovak_Republic: in Bohemia, Moravia and Silesia 39% of the population worked in industry and 31% in agriculture and forestry; Slovakia and Ruthenia were mainly agricultural. Czechoslovakia had inherited 70-80% of Austria-Hungary's industry.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment (s = 1 assumed). Czech lands 31% agriculture and forestry (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Czechoslovak_Republic); Slovakia and Ruthenia assumed ~60% (not fetched). Weighted by population (10.9M / 4.4M): ~39% -> 0.61. Roughly self-sufficient in grain and a sugar exporter.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching military age (21) per year: the 1917 birth cohort, depressed by the First World War (pre-war births ~30 per 1,000 of ~13.5M, roughly halved in 1915-18), half male, ~75% survival.

armor.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): LT vz.35 deliveries 15 (1936), 262 (1937), 21 (1938) for the army, plus export tanks for Iran, Peru, Switzerland and others from CKD and Skoda (high). Mid = the 1937 peak.

aircraft_fighter.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): B.534 / Bk.534 deliveries 100 (1935), 149 (1936), 174 (1937); 568 built in all. Range spans the 1936-37 rates.

aircraft_strike.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): Letov S.328 445 built 1935-39 (~90 a year), Aero MB.200 124 built (1936), Avia B-71 (licence SB) 161 built 1937-39; ~150 bombers and reconnaissance-bombers a year combined.

artillery.note: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Czechoslovakia 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle series and Osprey MAA 554 Czechoslovak Armies 1918-45): 37 mm vz.37 AT guns 1,131 built 1937-39 (~450 a year), 150 mm vz.25 345 (1930-39), 100 mm vz.30 188 (1932-39), 105 mm vz.35 106 (1935-39); field and AT pieces combined ~250-700 a year.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. State, district and municipal roads with hard surfaces; dense in Bohemia-Moravia, sparse in Slovakia and Ruthenia.

railKm.note: CHAT railline Czechoslovakia: 1936 = 13,595 km (high), 1937 = 13,548 km (low, mid); no 1938 value.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Landlocked. Danube port of Bratislava and the leased Czechoslovak zone in the port of Hamburg (Versailles treaty) were the only water outlets; neither can supply a fleet.

merchantTonnage.note: League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40, Table 113 (merchant vessels of 100 GRT and more, June 1929-1938) lists no Czechoslovak fleet; the first sea-going ships came in the 1950s.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Defensive war on interior lines from a dense railway net; 26,000 motor vehicles gave more reach than the Polish army had.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Low = 217,000 horses with the mobilised army (cited samlib page); national horse stock of roughly 0.6-0.8M guessed.

chokepoints: Ore Mountains and Bohemian Forest passes
Narrow Moravian waist after the Anschluss

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: mountain rim, a new fortified line and population support among Czechs and Slovaks; low 1.1 because the fortified borderlands were German-speaking and Austria (annexed March 1938) outflanked the line from the south.

notes: Snapshot date 30 September 1938: general mobilisation of 23 September complete, the day the Munich Agreement was signed. Territory and population are the pre-Munich republic (Sudetenland and Carpathian Ruthenia included); the world_1938 basemap already shows the reduced state, so the border uses the world_1930 polygon. Personnel: active = the mobilised army and air force (1.28M, range 0.97-1.5M); no navy. Equipment counts come from a samlib.ru compilation (Temezhnikov) that cites Shishkin's 1938 order-of-battle articles and Osprey MAA 554; they agree with the fort counts of the Wikipedia fortifications article. P-role counts are reconstructions from the division structure (grade D). Weakest values: the P-role split, support personnel, roads and horses (educated guesses). Ship convention per SOURCES.md: no ship roles, since the river flotilla cannot reach the sea.
